items.title: LXD: SSRF via image import from URL allows internal network probing by authenticated users
items.summary: ## Summary The LXD image import-from-URL endpoint (`POST /1.0/images` with `source.type=url`) makes server-side HTTP requests to an attacker-supplied URL without any private-IP or loopback blocking. items.title: listmonk: SQL Injection in `/api/subscribers/export` bypasses table access control, leaking admin password hashes and SMTP credentials
items.summary: ### Summary A SQL injection vulnerability in `GET /api/subscribers/export` allows an authenticated user with the `subscribers:sql_query` permission to bypass the table access control that exists on the regular query endpoint (`GET /api/subscribers`) and read arbitrary tables from the database — including `users` (bcrypt password hashes) and `settings` (SMTP credentials, API keys). Both error-based and time-based exfiltration techniques are confirmed to work. This creates a privilege escalation p

items.title: OSAC operator: Kubeconfig credential-plugin execution and SSRF in console proxy
items.summary: ### Impact The console-proxy's RemoteConfigResolver parses kubeconfig data from Kubernetes Secrets using clientcmd.RESTConfigFromKubeConfig without sanitizing the resulting rest.Config. A kubeconfig containing an exec plugin stanza (under users[].user.exec) is faithfully preserved. When rest.TransportFor later builds the HTTP transport for the upstream WebSocket connection, client-go invokes the exec plugin — spawning an arbitrary process as the osac-console-proxy service account. items.title: filecoin-pin: Unbounded DAG pinning can exhaust server resources
items.summary: ## Summary The IPFS Pinning Service API implementation accepts a caller-controlled CID through `POST /pins`, queues background processing, and then recursively fetches the full DAG with `helia.pins.add(cid)`. The route and background pinning path do not enforce a request rate limit, per-user quota, maximum DAG byte count, maximum block count, traversal timeout, or concurrent pinning limit. items.title: Banks: Unsafe importlib.import_module of attacker-controlled Tool.import_path in CompletionExtension allows RCE
items.summary: ## Summary `banks` parses `Tool` JSON objects from the rendered body of `{% completion %}` blocks and later resolves their `import_path` field through `importlib.import_module(...)` + `getattr(...)` to obtain the callable that handles a tool call. There is no allowlist or sanitization on `import_path`, so any importable Python attribute (e.g. `os.system`, `subprocess.getoutput`) can be selected. items.title: kaniko can send the build's Azure (Entra ID) access token to lookalike ACR registry hosts
items.summary: ### Summary kaniko before v1.25.20 can send a Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) access token for Azure Resource Manager to a registry host an attacker controls. A Dockerfile that references an image on a lookalike host, such as `FROM x.azurecr.io.attacker.com/img`, is enough. The build needs no `RUN` instruction and never has to push. The flaw is in the Azure Container Registry (ACR) credential helper, `github.com/chrismellard/docker-credential-acr-env`. kaniko links it into the executor and warmer

items.title: lxd allows Cross-guest volume hijack via DevLXD device patch
items.summary: ### Summary A guest can mount another guest's custom storage volume over `/dev/lxd` and read or write its contents without owning it. The DevLXD storage API blocks access to volumes you don't own, but the instance device-update path that attaches a volume to a container without checks ownership. Any guest in a project with `security.devlxd.management.volumes` enabled can attach a volume belonging to a different guest by naming it in a device `PATCH`, giving one tenant full read and write access
